newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official says nuclear cuts would aid Russia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official says nuclear cuts would aid Russia.

text.p: Russia's ratification of deeper nuclear weapons cuts would avoid a U.S. advantage in nuclear warheads and free money for Russia's cash-starved military, a U.S. defence official said on Friday.

He made the argument at a briefing on Defence Secretary William Perry's trip to Russia next week, which will include an address to the Russian Duma on Thursday largely to urge its ratification of the Start-2 strategic arms reduction treaty.
The treaty, already approved by the U.S. Senate but in trouble in the Duma, would cut U.S. and Russian nuclear warheads to 3,500 or less each.

The U.S. official, who briefed reporters on condition he not be identified, said Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov wanted to cut nuclear weapons to free money for the rest of his military but "in the absence of Start-2, we're certainly going to stay at Start-1 levels." That would keep U.S. nuclear forces at about 6,000 warheads.
The official said analysts doubted Russia could afford to maintain its arsenal at Start-1 levels for more than about two years, meaning its number of warheads would decline.
"If we stay roughly at Start-1 levels and economic pressures force the Russians down lower, clearly it's in their advantage as well as ours to come down to Start-2," he said.
But he said Russian ratification of Start-2 was in doubt.
"Start 2 is clearly in some degree of difficulty," he said. "Ratification is not certain if you took a look at the votes now."

"We're certainly not sending the secretary out to save a treaty which is otherwise sinking," he said. "But I think it is fair to say that what we hope to do is establish a factual basis for their further discussions."
